Circuit work

4 designs

A cross-section of the analog blocks I've designed — from the power stage down to the sub-circuits that keep it stable and self-referenced.

01

10 MHz multiphase DC-DC buck converter with DVFS

UMC 180nm. Full-chip tapeout with DVFS across 60 mV–2 V (1 V/ns reference transient, 0.7 V/μs tracking), a slew-enhancement mechanism achieving 38 mV undershoot / 35 mV overshoot at 1 A/ns load transient, and phase-current balancing across the multiphase power stage. VIN 2.8–3.3 V, VOUT 0.8–1.4 V, 100 mA–2 A load, 96% efficiency. Full-custom layout, IO/ESD ring integration, DRC/LVS/PEX and tapeout signoff.

02

3-stage capacitor-less nested Miller compensated LDO

UMC 180nm. 100 mA max load with a 100 pF output cap, 250 μA ultra-low quiescent current, 1 μA bias current. 100 dB DC gain, 84° phase margin at full load. VIN 1.4–1.8 V, regulated VOUT 1.2 V.

03

Bandgap reference with startup (ZTC)

SCL 180nm. Zero-temperature-coefficient reference at 27°C: Vref = 0.8 V, Iref = 50 μA. Supply sensitivity within ±5 mV/V over VDD = 1.8 V ±10%. 2 mW total power dissipation.

04

5-stage current-starved ring oscillator (VCO)

SCL 180nm. 30–70 MHz tuning range, KVCO of 60–90 MHz/V, voltage-controlled biasing with stage delay optimized for 10 fF parasitic capacitance per stage. Near rail-to-rail output swing, stable across the tuning range.
